subject: botany_2
question_text: Name any two essential elements and the deficiency diseases caused by them.

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.50, printed question 154. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. BOOK NOTE: the guide answers "Deficiency of N and K in plants cause a disease called Chlorosis", giving one symptom for both elements. Nitrogen deficiency does cause chlorosis; potassium deficiency causes MOTTLED chlorosis with marginal necrosis of the leaves. The card names both correctly and records the guide's single label. Examiner audit revision (2026-09-05): the first mistakes entry no longer says that only nitrogen deficiency gives chlorosis, because NCERT lists chlorosis under N, K, Mg, S, Fe, Mn, Zn and Mo; it now asks for the fuller symptom that identifies potassium.

insider_note: Name the element and its own symptom. Giving one symptom for two different elements is the guide's own shortcut and is not worth copying.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Two essential elements
steps.margin_note: Two named elements with symbols. Add the word macronutrient.
lines: Both are macronutrients, needed in large
steps.why: Both are macronutrients, so their shortage shows quickly and visibly — which is why they are the standard pair for this question.
common_mistakes: Naming a micronutrient and calling it a macronutrient. N and K are MACROnutrients.
Naming only one element. The question asks for two.
steps.memory_tip: N and K: the two the plant needs most and misses first.

steps.label: Their deficiency symptoms
steps.margin_note: One symptom per element, each defined in a few words.
lines: yellowing of leaves from loss of chlorophyll.
and NECROSIS of the leaf tips and margins.
steps.why: Each element has a different role in the plant, so each has a symptom of its own. Chlorosis fits several elements, so the extra detail is what identifies potassium.
common_mistakes: Stopping at the same one-word symptom for both. Nitrogen deficiency gives chlorosis; potassium deficiency gives mottled chlorosis with necrosis of the leaf tips and margins.
Defining chlorosis nowhere. One line saying it is the yellowing of leaves earns the mark.
steps.memory_tip: Yellow all over is nitrogen; dead edges are potassium.
